Dear Editor,

Please consider our manuscript, *Diagnosed but untreated: the national depression and anxiety treatment gap and its socioeconomic and insurance patterning in Kenya*, for publication as a Research Article.

KDHS 2022 is the first nationally representative Kenyan survey to carry a mental-health module. Published analyses of that module have described the prevalence and correlates of diagnosed depression and anxiety; none has used the survey's *treatment* item. Among 31,354 adults asked the module, we find that 3.6% reported a diagnosis of depression or anxiety, and that among those 1,091 adults, 75.3% (95% CI 71.9% to 78.7%) were not receiving treatment.

The central result is the contrast between two gradients. Diagnosis is modestly concentrated among wealthier and better-educated adults (concentration index 0.045), consistent with unequal access to recognition. The treatment gap, by contrast, is distribution-neutral (concentration index -0.003) and near-universal: 73.0% among the insured and 73.1% in the richest quintile, with no covariate strongly predictive after adjustment. This is the signature of a supply-side deficit rather than one that demand-side measures such as insurance enrolment would resolve — a distinction that matters directly for how Kenya invests under the Social Health Authority and the Mental Health (Amendment) Act 2022.

The manuscript is original, is not under consideration elsewhere, and uses authorised de-identified survey microdata. All authors have approved the submission and declare no competing interests.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Nichodemus Werre Amollo
Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology
